messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency SLO breach detected for model gptx-int8 in us-west-2. p95=850ms, p99=2.4s (SLO p99=1.2s). Error rate low but streaming stalls observed. Paging on-call now.
sara_oncall: on it. pulling dashboards and traces. any recent deploys or config changes?
mike_runtime: I'm seeing a calibration rollout completed ~10m ago for the int8 profile (calib v3 -> v4) on the model pool.
sanjay_mle: that calibration changed quantization thresholds and enabled a new dequant path for long-context batches. could be related.
kai_infra: adding raw tail traces: kv cache miss spikes correlate with the p99 windows. tails line up with cache eviction events.
lucy_cs: any customer-impact yet? CS got one support ticket reporting slow streaming responses in app session. probably a large customer in us-west.
sara_oncall: okay, triage plan: 1) confirm scope (model pool, region), 2) quick rollback to previous calib profile or force fallback to fp32 for streaming routes, 3) mitigate routing (shift traffic to hot pool), 4) notify CS.
mike_runtime: confirmed: affected pool = redwood-pool-gptx-12-int8, region us-west-2. ~17% of total streaming capacity.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Deployment: calib-service finished rollout 3110011950 -> calib-v4 to redwood-pool-gptx-12-int8.
sara_oncall: mike, can you dump a sample logs snippet where stall shows up?
mike_runtime: copy paste of tail:```[2026-03-15T17:13:22Z] request id=rxk9 kt=stream seq=1024 latency=2350ms stall=true kv_cache_hit=false kernel=dequant_v2```

```[2026-03-15T17:13:23Z] request id=rxkA kt=stream seq=128 latency=2400ms stall=true kernel=dequant_v2```

Looks like dequant_v2 path takes >2s when kv_cache_hit=false for long sequences.
sanjay_mle: that matches: calib-v4 tightened quant thresholds which reduced prefix sharing, increasing cache misses and triggering the slower dequant path.
kai_infra: current mitigation options: A) rollback calib-v4 -> v3; B) force routing to model-x-fp32 variant for streaming requests; C) enable prefix-KV forced retention (may increase memory). Which is fastest?
sara_oncall: B is quick but will increase cost; A needs deploy rollback (should be quick if we cancel rollout). C might be risky memory-wise. I vote A then B as fallback.
mike_runtime: I can cancel the calib rollout. command:```deployctl rollout cancel --service calib-service --target redwood-pool-gptx-12-int8 --to-version calib-v3``` will revert in ~3-5m.
sara_oncall: do it now, mike. notify if anything blocks.
mike_runtime: running cancel...

[deploy-bot]: rollback initiated for calib-service -> target redwood-pool-gptx-12-int8 (rollback id=rb-3110012018)
mike_runtime: rollback in progress, monitoring p99.
lucy_cs: letting impacted customer know we're aware and investigating. sending CS note: "We're investigating increased streaming latency in US-WEST; mitigation in progress."

10:48:12 monitor: p99 dropped to 1.9s (still above SLO).
sara_oncall: okay rollback is not fully propagated yet. if p99 not under SLO in 5m, implement B route fallback for streaming routes.

10:51:05 monitor: p99=1.25s, p95=780ms. trending down.

sanjay_mle: quick note: the dequant_v2 path uses a different kernel that is serialization heavy for long sequences. the calibration made more calls hit this path. once rollback completes, kernel selection will revert.
mike_runtime: rollback finished at 3110012175. p99 now 920ms.
sara_oncall: great. now run a short soak to confirm stability for 15m. keep monitoring logs for any residual stalls.

11:05:00 monitor: p99 steady at 880ms, p95 700ms. no more stall=true logs.
lucy_cs: updated customer: latency recovered, we rolled back an internal calibration change and are monitoring. they appreciated the update.

sanjay_mle: follow-ups: 1) put calib-v4 behind gradual canary with synthetic long-context load tests; 2) add pre-deploy perf gate for kernel path latency under high-miss scenarios; 3) ensure fallback routing can be toggled faster.
sara_oncall: add to postmortem: root cause = calibration change (calib-v4) increased cache misses -> triggered slow dequant kernel for long streaming sequences -> p99 SLO breach.
mike_runtime: quick mitigation doc snippet to add to runbook:```If p99 spikes after calib rollout: 1) cancel rollout 2) if rollback delayed, set streaming routes to fallback-model=fp32 var for region 3) increase KV retention temporarily until rollback completes```

lucy_cs: action item for CS: compile list of customers who hit >2s and reach out with timeline.

kai_infra: ops request: throttle future calib rollouts to 5% canary with long-seq synthetic traffic for 30m. put in release checklist.
sara_oncall: agreed. I'll open incident ticket and schedule postmortem with eng-ml and runtime tomorrow. tagging owners: @sanjay_mle, @mike_runtime, @kai_infra, @lucy_cs.

deploy-bot: incident ticket created: INC-311001-quant-calib-tail-rollback.
sara_oncall: closing paging loop — monitoring continues. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: NOTE: no data exfiltration or errors, only latency. severity: P2.

mike_runtime: logging final metrics to incident ticket and saving trace dump for postmortem.
sanjay_mle: moving forward I'll add a perf test against dequant_v2 path with mocked cache-miss distribution. want to prevent surprises.
sara_oncall: thanks everyone. postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow.

lucy_cs: customer follow-up scheduled.

ops-bot: Incident closed to on-call, keep channel for postmortem discussion if needed. :white_check_mark:
